import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture relating two characterizations of a set of integers.

Informal Statement:
For an integer $k \ge 2$, the following are equivalent:

1. The greatest common divisor of the binomial coefficients
    $\binom{2k}{k}, \binom{3k}{k}, \dots, \binom{(k+1)k}{k} = 1$.

2. Writing prime factorization of $k$ as
    $k = \prod p_i^{e_i}$, and let
    $P = \max_i p_i^{e_i}$,
    one has $k / P > P$.

This conjecture asserts that the sequence defined by 1. is obtained by
taking 1 off each number in the sequence defined by 2.

*References:*
- [A80170](https://oeis.org/A80170)
- [A51283](https://oeis.org/A51283)
-/

namespace OeisA80170

/--
The gcd of the binomial coefficients
$\binom{2k}{k}, \binom{3k}{k}, \dots, \binom{(k+1)k}{k} = 1$.
-/
def A (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (Finset.range k).gcd (fun i => Nat.choose ((i + 2) * k) k) = 1

/--
Let $P$ be the largest prime power dividing `k`.
Then $k / P > P$.
-/
def B (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  let P := ((Nat.divisors k).filter IsPrimePow).max.getD 0
  k / P > P

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : ¬A 2 := by unfold A; decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : ¬A 3 := by unfold A; decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : ¬A 4 := by unfold A; decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : ¬A 5 := by unfold A; decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_6 : ¬A 6 := by unfold A; decide

/--
Conjecture: The gcd condition is equivalent to the prime power condition.
This has been conjectured by Ralf Stephan.

Both the natural-language proof and its Lean 4 formalization were carried out
by the KLMM MechMath Agent Team; see the `formal_proof` attribute.

*References:*
- [Ralf Stephan, *Prove or Disprove. 100 Conjectures from the OEIS*, 2004, Conjecture 17 (arXiv:math/0409509)](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0409509)
- [Dakai Guo et al., *A Greatest Common Divisor Criterion of Certain Binomial Coefficients*, 2026 (arXiv:2606.22997)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22997)
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/guodk/formal-conjectures/blob/0720658844d76a50d48e4baa152eef14d4462907/FormalConjectures/OEIS/80170.lean#L1823"]
theorem gcdCondition_iff_primePowerCondition (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    A k ↔ B (k + 1) := by
  sorry

end OeisA80170

findings.description: The module docstring at lines 23–31 says that, for the same k ≥ 2, the gcd condition A k is equivalent to the prime-power condition B k. The source instead relates A k to B (k + 1), as the Lean theorem correctly does. The unshifted prose is false: A 29 ∧ ¬B 29 was proved independently in the scratch file. This is a documentation error only; the definitions and theorem should not be changed.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A080170 explicitly states “a(n) = A051283(n) - 1” (Ralf Stephan, Feb 20 2004), while A051283 defines the prime-power condition at its own input. Read via https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A080/A080170.seq and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A051/A051283.seq. Guo et al., arXiv:2606.22997, Theorem 1, likewise explicitly sets n = k + 1 and asserts D(k) = 1 iff n/ppart(n) > ppart(n).
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce the two numbered conditions as separate predicates A(k) and B(k), rather than saying they are equivalent at the same input. Then explicitly state: “For k ≥ 2, A(k) holds if and only if B(k + 1) holds.” This also makes the existing sequence-shift sentence consistent. Leave the Lean declarations unchanged.

reformulations.difference: Lean maximizes over all prime-power divisors, rather than just the full prime-power components in the prime factorization, and uses natural-number division.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For k ≥ 2 the filtered divisor set is nonempty. Every prime-power divisor p^j satisfies j ≤ v_p(k), so p^j ≤ p^v_p(k); conversely, every full component p^v_p(k) belongs to the filter. Thus both maxima are identical. This maximum P is positive and divides k, so natural-number division is exact and agrees with rational division. The maximum equality and the equivalence between B k and the source's rational quotient condition were proved in /workspace/review/bridges.lean, without sorry dependencies.

reformulations.difference: The OEIS comment gives an identity between enumerated sequence terms, A080170(n) = A051283(n) − 1; Lean states the pointwise membership equivalence A k ↔ B (k + 1).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The pointwise equivalence says exactly that translation by +1 maps the first sequence's support onto the second's. Translation preserves order, so their increasing enumerations differ by 1, and conversely the enumerated identity gives this membership equivalence. The restriction k ≥ 2 omits no terms: A 0 and A 1 are false, as are B 0, B 1, and B 2. The 2026 paper states the same pointwise formulation explicitly.

review.notes: Checked both definitions, all five test theorems, and the main theorem. Computations for inputs 0 through 200 matched the OEIS prefixes and found no failures of A k ↔ B (k + 1). Independent Lean proofs verified the gcd indexing and prime-power definition bridges. The linked proof was successfully rebuilt in scratch with only its legacy import path updated and namespace renamed; both its theorem and a direct application to the reviewed statement depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. OEIS A080170's June 29, 2026 comment confirms the proof, so the solved status is current. Stephan's original display (17) has apparent typesetting slips (a sum instead of a product and endpoint (n−1)n); the OEIS definitions and the explicit 2026 theorem unambiguously support the Lean statement. Direct OEIS pages were blocked, so their full entries were read through the official data mirror.
